evidence: Author uploaded stochastic_uncertainty_summary.json after completing fixed-mask five-seed run in audit_2006_stochastic_reconstruction.py
inference: Fixed-mask diffusion randomness yields low within-sector RMSE variability relative to reconstruction error. Dominant disagreement with SSUSI is not explained by sampling seed variation.
The observed hidden flux values fall within the 5-draw empirical 10%–90% envelope only 11.35% on average across 12 equally weighted acquisitions, showing limited observed-target inclusion.

The finite-five-draw order statistic envelope is not a calibrated 80% predictive interval, so do not apply an 80%-nominal significance claim or equate this inclusion to predictive uncertainty calibration.

Single-draw January 2006 primary RMSE 0.661641975 and all paired DDPM/OVATION/interpolation baseline results remain the main publication inference; 0.662220 is a supplemental average across five seeds, not a replacement primary benchmark.
The 12 January 2006 acquisition clusters may share geomagnetic disturbances; sector/pixel-level samples cannot be treated as 36 or thousands of independent storms.

Five random seeds and single month are limited; stochastic sampling spread is only one source of predictive uncertainty (not observations, training distribution shift, or model-structure uncertainty).
The real extreme hard case REV11610 is preserved in the main uncertainty and primary error analyses.
